# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 6 (PNEUMA Dynamic)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 6
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. When he gave this commandment, what did he say? "Who is the one picking a fight with me? Let them stand up and face me. Who wants to take me to court? Let them come before the Lord's servant."
2. "A curse on all of you — you will wear out like old clothing, and the moths will eat you."
3. The prophet also speaks in another place, setting Christ as a crushing stone: "I am laying a precious stone in Zion — chosen, honored, a cornerstone — and whoever trusts in him will live forever."
4. So — is our hope built on a literal stone? Of course not. He made his flesh into something strong. That is what he means when he says: "He set me as a hard rock."
5. The prophet says again: "The stone the builders threw away — that stone became the cornerstone." And: "This is the great and wonderful day that the Lord has made."
6. I am writing plainly so you can follow; I am a poor servant to you in love.
7. Look at what it says: "He set me as a hard rock." What rock, what stone? Here is what scripture says: "I am placing the Word in Zion — a stone that trips people up, a boulder that causes them to stumble. But whoever believes in him will never be disgraced."
8. The Lord's flesh had to suffer. His appearance in the flesh meant this: so that death's claim on the flesh could be canceled, and those who were rotting away could be made holy through the forgiveness of sins — through the sprinkling of his blood.
9. What scripture says about him applies partly to Israel and partly to us: "He was wounded for our sins and crushed for our iniquities. Through his bruise we were healed."
10. Do you see it? His stripes were our healing; our sins were taken away.
11. What does the prophet mean, then, by saying: "I entered the good land that the Lord promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and he gave it to us as our inheritance — a land flowing with milk and honey"?
12. Understand: knowledge is the word of wisdom; understanding is the teachings of the word; and instruction is the commandments. These are what make up the pleasant land — the one flowing with milk and honey.
